## Independence and scope

Formal-lifecycle/manual independent milestone reassessment. Separate distribution-code-reviewer authored none of the implementation, tests or report; parent distribution-implementer authored first pass and correction. Handoff a7ae0897 corrects c56ddae5; complete M1 is reviewed against approved checkpoint 2520313b, current design-review-r5 and delivery-review-r2. Exact engineering subjects below include the helper, direct tests, two existing-test corrections and implementation report. Public dispatch and old managed helper remain unchanged. No published skill text changed.

Reviewer inspected the complete first-pass helper/tests, current correction diff and report, and preserved governing/command basis. Fresh exact identities confirm upstream Design/plan and approved review evidence are unchanged. First-pass judgment and finding origins remain historical; only reporter dispositions and fresh r2 are recorded. Source, plan, work and routing are untouched by this reviewer.

## Checklist assessment

1. Spec alignment: pass for isolated M1. Actual two-parent /proc descriptor anchoring, preflight snapshots, outside-discovery retention, no-clobber publication and safe capability stop implement the selected internal primitive. Discovery aliases now reject rather than bypass containment. No project-state reader, recovery schema or public force dispatch is introduced.
2. Test coverage: pass. Focused tests cover real supported move, directory/file replacement, default empty/identical conflicts, complete conflict stop, new arrivals, source/ancestor changes, symlinks/unsafe paths, unavailable anchoring, retained old-handle writes, configured alias rejection and real partial multi-unit publication. The missing proof finding is directly repaired.
3. Edge cases: pass within M1. Discovery checking handles existing aliases and absent roots beneath aliases; reviewer also exercised a nonoverlapping absent configured root successfully. Partial outcomes identify completed, failed and untouched units with no later-unit installation; default retry preserves an independent edit. Explicit force continues to replace only verified candidate units.
4. Error handling: pass. Opened descriptors are closed, no-clobber publication preserves competing destinations, failures retain detached originals, and no automatic rollback overwrites independent work. No real cross-mount fixture was available; the opened-parent device comparison was inspected, and the required unavailable-capability failure path was executed. This is a disclosed cross-mount execution limitation, not a claimed test result.
5. Architecture boundaries: pass. Helper remains internal, Node-only and independent of project-state/adoption/publication authority. Anchored roots and retention parents are distinct from arbitrary input path spelling. Known Linux support is demonstrated; unsupported descriptor-relative access rejects rather than silently falling back.
6. Compatibility: pass for this milestone. Existing public behavior and managed consumers remain unchanged and author full npm proof passes. Existing-test corrections respect Release-owned generated candidate metadata and preserve historical digest and actual CLI status projection. Real candidate replacement proof is now executed before M1 closeout.
7. Security/privacy: pass for inspected scope. Non-following opens, actual discovery ancestor checks, private outside-root retention and exclusive publication maintain the selected mutation boundary. No secrets, network calls or wider external permissions are added. Continued late old-inode writes remain preserved, not excluded by an overbroad concurrency claim.
8. Derived artifact currency: pass within M1 limits. No source skills, public dispatch or current release metadata are changed. Executed Release candidate proof establishes the existing retained test boundary only; M2 must repeat affected proof after its public support changes.
9. Unrelated changes: pass. Two existing-test repairs are bounded to reproduced pre-change failures and do not change production observability or Release. Admission/retirement evidence names their current owners and replacement observation boundaries. No installed runtime cleanup occurred.
10. Validation evidence: pass with stated limitations. Author focused13/full npm477 and real candidate proof are current to the correction. Reviewer independently ran focused13 and the alias/nonoverlap script. Frozen baseline results establish the original failures; timing differences are disclosed rather than presented as controlled performance gains. No broad extra suite was required for this rereview.

## Finding dispositions

Finding ID: dist-m1-discovery-alias

The helper now inspects every configured discovery root through its existing ancestors and rejects realpath aliases, including a missing child below a symlink; checks repeat during parent validation before mutation. Added direct regressions preserve the original. Reviewer reran the original alias reproduction: aliasBlocked=true, then a legitimate nonoverlapping configured root completed with its original retained. This meets the original containment/rejection outcome.

Finding ID: dist-m1-partial-proof

A file-published checkpoint now interrupts a real partially populated multi-file skill after an earlier unit completes and before a later unit begins. The test verifies exact completed/failed/untouched lists, present and absent candidate bytes, retained original content, and preservation of an independent edit on default retry. Existing complete force-directory tests cover explicit replacement of such arbitrary existing content. Evidence no longer relies solely on interruption after a complete unit.

Finding ID: dist-m1-retirement-evidence

The author executed exact archived pre-change 0d3fd0b6 source: 462/464 tests reproduced the two original baseline failures. Real ReleaseCandidateIntegrationTests.test_actual_candidate_build_and_packed_metadata_chain passed in M1, observing generation/archive/metadata/packed-install rather than deferring replacement proof. Historical digest and actual concise exit projection remain tested. TG-08 report distinguishes this reconstructed baseline from pre-authoring measurement, records command/changed-line/owner scope, and explicitly discloses differing timing sources/no speedup claim. Missing pre-authoring timing cannot be recreated, but frozen pre-change execution and current results satisfy the bounded factual comparison without inventing an execution or waiver.

## Exact verification and limits

Reviewer command node --test packages/rigorloop/test/installer-replacement.test.js passed 13/13, zero failures, 109.935922 ms. Reviewer node --input-type=module temporary-filesystem reproduction returned aliasBlocked=true, nonoverlapCompleted=1 and retainedOriginal=true. No reviewed-source mutation occurred.

Author reports npm test --prefix packages/rigorloop passed477/477 in23930.267666ms; exact frozen-baseline run passed462/464 with the two expected historical failures in20.929814s; python3 scripts/test-release-transaction.py ReleaseCandidateIntegrationTests.test_actual_candidate_build_and_packed_metadata_chain passed in98.598s. Baseline was reconstructed after authoring from exact source and timing methods differ, so there is no controlled speedup claim. Actual cross-mount execution is not claimed. Final integrated product behavior belongs to M2–M4 and later whole-change review/Verify.

## Handoff

No required M1 finding remains. Return approval to Route for the next in-scope implementation milestone M2, not final closeout. This assessment closes only M1 and does not claim CI, branch, PR or Verify readiness, adoption, user-runtime replacement or publication. Final whole-change Code Review and distinct Verify remain mandatory after all milestones and corrections.
